concepts.summary: A transformation of the fields that leaves the action invariant with a parameter constant over spacetime. Symmetries are classified as internal or spacetime, discrete or continuous, and global or local (gauge).

concepts.name: Global U(1) phase symmetry and its current
aliases: phase rotation of a complex field
concepts.summary: Multiplying a complex field by a constant phase leaves its free Lagrangian invariant. The associated conserved current is i(phi d phi* - phi* d phi) up to sign conventions, whose charge counts particles minus antiparticles after quantization.

concepts.name: O(N) and Z_2 symmetric scalar models
concepts.summary: N real scalar fields with a Lagrangian that depends only on the sum of squares are invariant under rotations of the field vector by O(N); a single real field with an even potential has the discrete Z_2 symmetry phi -> -phi.

concepts.name: Noether's theorem
concepts.summary: If a continuous transformation changes the Lagrangian by at most a total derivative, the field equations imply a conserved current built from the variation of the fields; it fails for discrete symmetries and holds on shell.

concepts.name: Conserved current and charge
concepts.summary: A vector field J^mu with vanishing divergence; its time component integrated over space is a charge that is constant in time when no flux escapes through spatial infinity.

concepts.name: Energy-momentum tensor
concepts.summary: The four conserved currents associated with spacetime translations, collected into a tensor whose 00 component is the energy density and 0i components the momentum density; its spatial integrals are the conserved energy and momentum.

concepts.name: Improvement of the stress tensor
concepts.summary: Adding the divergence of a tensor antisymmetric in its first two indices leaves a conserved energy-momentum tensor conserved and the total charges unchanged; this freedom is used to make the tensor symmetric.

concepts.name: Conjugate momentum and field Hamiltonian
aliases: Legendre transform of a field Lagrangian
concepts.summary: For each field the conjugate momentum density is the derivative of the Lagrangian density with respect to the field's time derivative; the Hamiltonian is the spatial integral of momentum times velocity minus the Lagrangian density.

concepts.name: Canonical quantization of fields
concepts.summary: Promoting a field and its conjugate momentum to operators with canonical commutators; for a free field each Fourier mode becomes an independent harmonic oscillator, and its excitations are interpreted as particles.

concepts.name: Equal-time commutation relations
concepts.summary: At equal times the field and its conjugate momentum have commutator i times a three-dimensional delta function, while fields commute with fields and momenta with momenta.

concepts.name: Creation and annihilation operators
concepts.summary: Operators a and a-dagger with [a, a-dagger] = 1, or (2 pi)^3 delta^3 per momentum mode, that lower and raise oscillator occupation numbers; the number operator a-dagger a counts excitations.

concepts.name: Mode expansion of a free field
aliases: field as integral over creation and annihilation operators
concepts.summary: Writing a free field as an integral over momenta of annihilation operators times positive-frequency plane waves plus creation operators times negative-frequency ones, with the on-shell energy and a factor 1/sqrt(2E).

concepts.name: Fock space
concepts.summary: The direct sum of n-particle state spaces generated by acting with creation operators on a vacuum annihilated by every annihilation operator; bosonic states are symmetric under exchange and particle number is not fixed.

concepts.name: Zero-point (vacuum) energy
concepts.summary: The free Hamiltonian contains half a quantum of energy per mode; summed over all modes this vacuum energy diverges. Only energy differences are observable without gravity, so the constant is usually removed by normal ordering.

concepts.name: Normal ordering
concepts.summary: Rearranging a product of free-field operators so that all creation operators stand to the left of all annihilation operators; the vacuum expectation of a nonconstant normal-ordered product vanishes.

concepts.name: Relativistic normalization of states
concepts.summary: One-particle momentum states normalized with a factor 2E_p times (2 pi)^3 delta^3, which makes the normalization Lorentz invariant and the completeness relation use the invariant measure; in a finite box delta^3(0) becomes V/(2 pi)^3.

concepts.name: Complex scalar field
concepts.summary: A complex-valued field, equivalent to two real fields of equal mass, with kinetic term |d phi|^2 and mass term m^2 |phi|^2; its quantization needs two independent sets of oscillators.

concepts.name: Antiparticle
concepts.summary: The second species of quanta of a complex field, created by the operator that accompanies the negative-frequency modes of the field; it has the same mass as the particle and opposite conserved U(1) charge.

concepts.name: Heisenberg picture
concepts.summary: The description in which operators carry the time dependence, evolving with the full Hamiltonian by conjugation with the evolution operator, while states are constant; for a free field the Heisenberg equation reproduces the classical field equation.

concepts.name: Interaction picture
concepts.summary: Splitting H = H_0 + H_int, operators evolve with H_0, so fields are free fields, and states evolve with the interaction Hamiltonian written in terms of those free fields.

concepts.name: Dyson series
concepts.summary: The interaction-picture evolution operator as the time-ordered exponential of minus i times the integrated interaction Hamiltonian, expanded order by order; time ordering replaces nested integrals by integrals over a full cube divided by n!.

concepts.name: Time-ordered product
concepts.summary: The product of field operators rearranged so that operators at later times stand to the left, written with step functions in the time differences; it is symmetric in its arguments for bosonic fields.

concepts.name: Wightman function
concepts.summary: The vacuum expectation of a product of two fields in a fixed operator order. For a free scalar it is an integral of plane waves over the invariant mass-shell measure; reversing the order gives its complex conjugate, and their difference is the commutator.

concepts.name: Retarded propagator
concepts.summary: The step function in the time difference times the vacuum commutator of two fields, up to a factor of i. It vanishes unless the second point lies in the past light cone of the first and solves the Klein-Gordon equation with a delta source; the advanced kernel has the opposite time support.

concepts.name: Feynman propagator
concepts.summary: The vacuum expectation of the time-ordered product of two free fields. In momentum space it is i/(p^2 - m^2 + i epsilon); the epsilon prescription moves the poles so that positive energies propagate forward in time, and it solves the Klein-Gordon equation with a -i delta source.

concepts.name: i-epsilon pole prescription
concepts.summary: Shifting singular denominators or times by an infinitesimal imaginary amount to choose how a contour passes the poles. The choice encodes boundary conditions: Feynman, retarded and advanced kernels differ only in where the poles are placed.

concepts.name: Microcausality
concepts.summary: Local observables at spacelike separation commute, so no measurement can signal faster than light. Correlation functions such as the Feynman propagator may still be nonzero outside the light cone.

concepts.name: Linear response to a source
concepts.summary: Coupling a field to an external source and expanding to first order expresses the change of an expectation value as the source integrated against the retarded commutator of the unperturbed theory.

concepts.name: Massless two-point function in d dimensions
concepts.summary: For a massless free scalar in d > 2 spacetime dimensions the Wightman function is a constant times 1/(x^2 - (t - i epsilon)^2)^(d/2 - 1); the epsilon selects the phase in timelike regions, and the two orderings agree at spacelike separation.

concepts.name: Correlation functions
aliases: Green's functions of the interacting theory
concepts.summary: Vacuum expectation values of time-ordered products of Heisenberg fields at several spacetime points; they are the basic observables from which scattering amplitudes are extracted.

concepts.name: Green's function
concepts.summary: A solution of a linear differential equation with a delta-function source, singled out by boundary or causal conditions; convolving it with a source gives the solution of the inhomogeneous equation, and in Fourier space it is the reciprocal of the operator's symbol.

concepts.name: Dirac delta
concepts.summary: The distribution that evaluates a test function at a point; formally the integral of plane waves over all momenta. It enforces conservation laws inside integrals, and squared deltas are interpreted with a finite volume and time, delta^3(0) = V/(2 pi)^3.

concepts.name: Yukawa potential
aliases: static Green's function of a massive field
concepts.summary: The static potential e^{-mr}/(4 pi r) produced by a point source of a massive field, found by Fourier transforming 1/(k^2 + m^2) and evaluating the integral by contour methods; it reduces to the Coulomb potential as m goes to 0.

concepts.name: Proca field
concepts.summary: A vector field with Maxwell kinetic term and mass term m^2 A^2 / 2; with a conserved source its equations of motion force partial_mu A^mu = 0, so three polarizations propagate.

concepts.name: Free electromagnetic field
concepts.summary: The vector potential with field strength F = dA and Lagrangian -F_{mu nu}F^{mu nu}/4, coupled to a conserved current; its static solution for a point charge is the Coulomb potential.

concepts.name: Old-fashioned perturbation theory
concepts.summary: Perturbation theory in a Hamiltonian split H_0 + V, using on-shell intermediate states and energy denominators (E - H_0 + i epsilon)^{-1}; energy is not conserved at vertices, and summing time orderings recovers covariant propagators.

concepts.name: S-matrix
concepts.summary: The operator mapping asymptotic incoming free states in the far past to outgoing states in the far future, equal to the interaction-picture evolution operator from minus to plus infinity; its matrix elements give transition amplitudes.

concepts.name: Unitarity of the S-matrix
concepts.summary: Probabilities summed over all outcomes are conserved, so the S-matrix and the evolution operator it comes from are unitary when the Hamiltonian is Hermitian.

concepts.name: Invariant amplitude
concepts.summary: The Lorentz-invariant quantity M left after writing S = 1 + iT and factoring the overall energy-momentum delta function out of <f|iT|i>; Feynman rules compute iM.

concepts.name: LSZ reduction formula
concepts.summary: Scattering amplitudes equal Fourier-transformed time-ordered correlation functions with each external propagator amputated by multiplying by (p^2 - m^2) and taking the momentum on shell, up to factors of the one-particle field normalization.

concepts.name: Wick's theorem
concepts.summary: A time-ordered product of free fields equals its normal-ordered product plus all ways of replacing disjoint pairs by Feynman propagators; the vacuum expectation is the sum over complete pairings and vanishes for an odd number of real fields.

concepts.name: Feynman diagrams
concepts.summary: Graphs that organize each term of a perturbative expansion: lines are propagators or contractions, vertices are interaction terms, and integrals run over vertex positions or internal momenta; each diagram stands for a definite integral.

concepts.name: Momentum-space Feynman rules
concepts.summary: Rules for writing iM from a diagram: a propagator i/(p^2 - m^2 + i epsilon) per internal line, the coupling times -i per vertex, momentum conservation at each vertex, an integral over each undetermined loop momentum, and symmetry factors.

concepts.name: Symmetry factor
concepts.summary: In a factorial-normalized scalar perturbation expansion, a diagram carries the factor 1/S, where S counts relabellings of vertices and their incident half-edges that preserve the Wick pairing and fix the labelled external insertions.

concepts.name: phi^4 theory
concepts.summary: A single real scalar field with interaction -lambda phi^4/4!; its vertex joins four lines with factor -i lambda, the 4! cancelling the equivalent contractions of four identical fields.

concepts.name: phi^3 theory
concepts.summary: A single real scalar field with cubic interaction g phi^3/3!, the simplest model for tree-level exchange diagrams and one-loop corrections; its potential is unbounded below, so it serves only as a perturbative toy model.

concepts.name: Scalar Yukawa theory
aliases: real mediator coupled to a complex scalar
concepts.summary: A real scalar mediator coupled to a complex scalar through g phi chi* chi. The interaction preserves the U(1) of the complex field and permits decays of the mediator into a particle-antiparticle pair when kinematically allowed.

concepts.name: Derivative interactions
concepts.summary: Interaction terms containing derivatives of fields; in momentum space each derivative brings a factor of plus or minus i times the momentum of that leg, so the direction of momentum flow at a vertex matters. Integration by parts gives equivalent amplitudes.

concepts.name: Mandelstam variables
concepts.summary: For two-to-two scattering, the invariants s = (p1 + p2)^2, t = (p1 - p3)^2 and u = (p1 - p4)^2; their sum equals the sum of the four squared masses, and in the center-of-mass frame t and u carry the scattering angle.

concepts.name: s-, t- and u-channel exchange
concepts.summary: The tree diagrams in which two cubic vertices exchange a virtual particle, labelled by which Mandelstam invariant flows through the propagator; which channels contribute depends on the identity and charges of the external particles.

concepts.name: Loop diagrams and loop integrals
concepts.summary: Diagrams whose lines form closed cycles; each independent loop leaves an unconstrained internal momentum to integrate over, and a connected graph with I internal lines and V vertices has I - V + 1 loops.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet divergence and power counting
concepts.summary: The growth of a momentum integral at large momentum, estimated by comparing the powers of momentum in the measure and in the propagators and vertices; examples are the quartic vacuum-energy divergence and the logarithmic one-loop bubble in four dimensions.

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.summary: Temporarily modifying the theory at high energy, for example with a momentum cutoff, so that divergent integrals become finite; renormalization then expresses predictions in terms of measured parameters, after which they should not depend on the regulator.

concepts.name: Mass dimension of couplings
concepts.summary: In four dimensions a scalar field has mass dimension 1, so the coupling of phi^n has dimension 4 - n. Positive, zero and negative dimension classify interactions as relevant, marginal or irrelevant: relevant couplings dominate at low energy, irrelevant ones grow in importance at high energy, and marginal ones are classified by quantum corrections.

concepts.name: Vacuum bubbles
concepts.summary: Subdiagrams with no external points. Their sum factors out of every correlation function and exponentiates, and it is cancelled by the normalizing vacuum-to-vacuum amplitude.

concepts.name: Connected diagrams
concepts.summary: Diagrams in which every vertex is joined to every external point through lines. Disconnected pieces with external legs describe particles that do not interact; nontrivial amplitudes come from connected, amputated diagrams.

concepts.name: Interacting vacuum
concepts.summary: The ground state of the full Hamiltonian, which generally differs from the free vacuum; evolving a free state through a long, slightly imaginary time interval projects onto it when the overlap is nonzero.

concepts.name: Gell-Mann-Low formula
concepts.summary: Time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting vacuum equal the free-vacuum expectation of free fields times the time-ordered exponential of the integrated interaction, divided by the same expectation without the fields.

concepts.name: Schwinger-Dyson equations
aliases: quantum equations of motion for correlators
concepts.summary: Applying the free wave operator to a time-ordered correlation function gives the correlator with the classical equation of motion inserted plus delta-function contact terms from the canonical commutators.

concepts.name: Cross section
concepts.summary: The scattering rate divided by the incident flux, an effective area; the event rate is the luminosity times the cross section, and the Lorentz-invariant formula divides |M|^2 times final-state phase space by the flux factor.

concepts.name: Decay rate and lifetime
concepts.summary: The transition probability per unit time for an unstable particle, computed in its rest frame as |M|^2 times final-state phase space over twice its mass; partial widths add, and the lifetime is the inverse total width.

concepts.name: Lorentz-invariant phase space
concepts.summary: The final-state measure: a product of invariant one-particle measures times (2 pi)^4 times the energy-momentum delta function. For two bodies in the center-of-mass frame it reduces to an angular integral weighted by the final momentum over the total energy.

concepts.name: Fermi's golden rule
concepts.summary: A constant transition rate is obtained from the squared amplitude by replacing the square of the energy delta function with the observation time over 2 pi times one delta function and dividing by that time.

concepts.name: Breit-Wigner resonance
concepts.summary: An unstable particle's propagator acquires an imaginary part m Gamma in its denominator, giving a resonance peak in s-channel cross sections whose width is the decay rate; the imaginary part arises from loops of lighter particles into which it can decay.

concepts.name: Resummation of propagator insertions
concepts.summary: Chains of a two-point insertion between free propagators form a geometric series, which sums to a propagator with a shifted denominator; treating a mass term as an interaction and resumming reproduces the massive propagator.

concepts.name: Perturbative solution of classical field equations
concepts.summary: Solving a nonlinear field equation with a source order by order in the coupling by repeatedly convolving with the Green's function of the free operator; each term is drawn as a tree diagram with sources at its leaves.
